correctness.rationale: For three loopless balanced directed contacts every row and column stochastic matrix is A_p with clockwise rate p and reverse rate 1-p. Its Perron root is 1, so beta/gamma=b is fixed. Initially transmission before recovery has probability b/(1+b). After the second infection, two memoryless unit-recovery infectious individuals contact the remaining susceptible with rates bp and b(1-p); failure probability is 1/[(1+bp)(1+b(1-p))]. This yields P(K=1)=1/(1+b), P(K=2)=b/[(1+b)(1+b+b²p(1-p))], and P(K=3) the complement. The sole varying upper tail strictly increases with p(1-p), establishing first-order stochastic domination, extrema at p=0,1 and p=1/2. Extreme risk gap Delta=b³/[(1+b)²(b+2)²] has unique positive critical point b=(3+sqrt33)/2 and sharp maximum (33sqrt33-189)/8. Independently checked 20 exact rational Markov-state recursions. The competing-risk proof is valid for all b>0 and 0<=p<=1.

value.rationale: Epidemic networks with exactly the same reproduction-matrix Perron root can have differing exact final-outbreak risk. Scope is deliberately three individuals and independent exponential recovery.
